title: Transport Corporation of India Ltd - 532349 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: TCI Q2 FY27: revenue grew about 15% (consolidated 14.8%) while PAT stayed flat, with Seaways fuel-driven pricing and JV dividends lower.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as strong on the top line, with business growing about 14.85-15% and standalone revenue up about 10%, but bottom line did not keep pace. Growth was largely value-led, driven by freight rate increases passed through after higher diesel and bunker prices, plus new contracts. Standalone PAT was flat because joint venture profits and dividends were lower. Seaways took delivery of its first 500 TEU vessel (TCI Setu) just before the call, and capex of roughly Rs 300 crore in the half is weighing on ROCE and return on net worth.

financial_highlights.change: Management cited as high growth; standalone top line about 10%
Management said margins were up slightly
Driven by pricing after bunker price rise

segments.name: Freight (road/LTL/FTL)
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 12% in Q2 and 11.5% for H1; roughly two-thirds of growth from pricing and one-third from volume. EBIT declined, margins described as flat to low; 11 new offices opened.

segments.name: Seaways (coastal shipping)
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 28% on freight rate increases of about 10-15% against bunker price rise of about 20%. EBIT growth muted by fuel costs; management guides EBITDA margin of 35-40% (maybe 38%). First 500 TEU vessel TCI Setu delivered; second ship expected around early January.

segments.name: Supply chain solutions
segments.commentary: Grew about 10% off a higher base; strong contract pipeline in transport and warehousing. Margins slightly up; capex in warehouse equipment and trucks continuing.

segments.name: Concor JV
segments.commentary: Grew about 10.5% with profitability flat; outlook 10-15% growth.

segments.name: Cold chain JV
segments.commentary: Grew about 50% on quick commerce contracts; profitability roughly doubled versus full prior year; outlook about 40% growth.

segments.name: Transport JV
segments.commentary: Profitability slightly muted; outlook about 10-12% growth.

guidance_outlook: Top-line growth guided at 10-12%, with margins also guided in the 10-12% range; H2 expected to be stronger than H1.
Seaways: top line growth of 15-20% for FY27 and over 20% in FY28 as capacity rises about 17-18%; bottom line growth 10-15%.
Supply chain growth guided at 12-13% (teens) for FY27 with higher growth in FY28.
FY27 capex about Rs 500-550 crore per earlier guidance, with ship final payment also in the year; separate comment on about Rs 600 crore capex plan.
Depreciation expected to rise to about 2.6-2.7% of revenue from about 2.5%, a 10-15% increase on last year.
Net debt expected around Rs 150-200 crore by FY27 end, versus about Rs 90-100 crore now.
capex_capacity: Seaways: first ship (500 TEU, about 7,500 tonnes) taken delivery; operations expected to start by end-November after China-India voyage; second ship expected early January.
Seaways fleet about 78,000 DWT plus about 15,000 DWT from new ship; target about one lakh tonne by FY29-30. One small ship in dry dock mid-March next year; one already completed this year.
Seaways ships extended to FY30 for operational days previously expiring in FY28.
Adding one more railway rake this quarter; continued investment in trucks, warehouse equipment and handling systems (not real estate).
Capex of about Rs 300 crore in H1 was cited as weighing on ROCE and return on net worth; FY28 capex guidance likely next year.
demand_pricing: Freight rates raised by about 10-15% in Seaways against bunker price rise of about 20% (from Rs 70-80k to Rs 95-98k per tonne); pricing limited by customers shifting to rail.
Auto sector saw softer offtake ahead of festive season; pre-stocking continued but lower than last year, on a high base.
Quick commerce, electronics, high tech and heavy engineering cited as demand drivers; new RFQs bring cost pressure.
Seaways demand is primarily domestic; some opportunities on Colombo, Myanmar, Thailand and Indonesia routes.
Competition: VRL seen taking share in express and delivery; FTL margins compressed across the market.
DFC completion in June seen as partly shifting volumes from road but overall volume growth continuing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised Seaways margin, expected Seaways revenue for FY27 and FY28, and the effective tax rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to 35-40% EBITDA margin, with possible start-up losses on the first ship. Revenue growth about 15-20% in FY27; tax rate about 9.5-10% and expected to stay similar.

qa_highlights.question: Where will debt peak for FY28-29 and how will depreciation move?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt about Rs 90-100 crore now, expected Rs 150-200 crore at FY27 end; 20-25% of the capex plan to be externally funded. Depreciation rising to 2.6-2.7% of revenue, up 10-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the capex plan of Rs 1,000-1,200 crore over three years still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Rs 600 crore this year is largely spillover from earlier plans; new multi-year guidance likely with FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How much of freight revenue growth is pricing-led?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly two-thirds pricing and one-third volume in Q2, after diesel surcharges began to be passed on in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for supply chain demand and the auto sector?
qa_highlights.answer: Supply chain growth guided at 12-13% for FY27 with higher growth in FY28; auto offtake softer but pipeline in auto and warehousing strong.

risks_watch: Seaways margins exposed to bunker price volatility; freight rates could fall fast with overcapacity talk, and pricing may reverse.
Start-up losses and higher depreciation and finance cost from new ships.
Freight division share gains lag competitors; margin pressure from new RFQs and FTL compression.
JV dividend income lower; recovery expected in H2 needed to lift PAT.
Rising debt and reducing cash after Rs 150 crore buyback; promoter holding now around 70%.
Auto sector offtake softness after high base.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and capacity additions, but cautious on near-term margins, which management attributed to fuel costs, ship start-up and depreciation. Management was candid that PAT was flat and ROCE muted, and was openly unpredictable on shipping rates.
key_quotes: This has been an interesting quarter with good double-digit growth on the top line, though bottom line did not keep up with that same pace.
So, I would think that this 15 -20 percent kind of growth for the top line and about 10 -15 percent for the bottom line should continue with the addition of the new ship.
So we are very confident of achieving our guidance.

adds.what: 500 TEU (about 7,500 tonne) coastal vessel TCI Setu (Seaways), delivered; operations expected by end-November
Two 15,000 DWT Seaways ships (fleet capacity addition of ~17-18% combined with 7,500-ton ships)

growth.why: Management guides FY27 freight top-line growth of 10-12% and supply chain 12-13%, with Seaways top line 15-20% backed by two ships adding ~17-18% capacity, though much of Q2 growth was price-led from bunker pass-through and standalone PAT was flat.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides freight and supply chain margins flat to low, consolidated EBITDA margin about 8.3% in Q2, and depreciation rising to 2.6-2.7% of revenue from 2.5% plus start-up losses on new ships weigh on PAT; Seaways 35-40% EBITDA margin is exposed to bunker volatility (bunker up about 20%).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: First 500 TEU ship TCI Setu delivered with operations by end-November, second ship expected early January, and two 15,000 DWT ships planned around Q4 FY27 adding ~17-18% Seaways capacity; one railway rake added this quarter.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Freight volume is about one-third of the 12% Q2 revenue growth (roughly 4% volume), Concor JV guided at 10-15% and cold chain at about 40%, with DFC completion in June seen partly shifting volumes from road.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex of about Rs 300 crore in H1 against an FY27 budget of Rs 500-550 crore, and management said FY28 capex guidance and new multi-year plan (versus Rs 1,000-1,200 crore over three years) likely comes with FY28; Seaways target of about one lakh tonne by FY29-30 needs further ships.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Freight top-line guidance held at 10-12% against H1 growth of 11.5% and standalone PAT flat; Seaways FY27 revenue guided 15-20% with pricing reversal risk on overcapacity talk.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Freight margins described as flat to low, FTL margins compressing and VRL taking share, JV dividends lower with H2 recovery needed, and freight rates could fall fast if Seaways pricing reverses after bunker pass-through.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Seaways new ships and possible Colombo, Myanmar, Thailand and Indonesia routes are mentioned, but no firm new service or product launch date was given.

rows.label: Supply chain contract pipeline
rows.why: Supply chain grew about 10% in Q2 with a strong pipeline in transport and warehousing, supporting guided 12-13% FY27 growth with higher growth in FY28.

rows.label: Net debt rising to Rs 150-200 crore
rows.why: Net debt rises from about Rs 90-100 crore now to Rs 150-200 crore by FY27 end after the Rs 150 crore buyback and ship payments, with 20-25% of capex to be externally funded.

rows.label: Seaways freight rate reversal risk
rows.why: Freight rates were raised 10-15% against a bunker rise of about 20% (Rs 70-80k to Rs 95-98k per tonne), and management was openly unpredictable on shipping rates amid overcapacity talk.

tone.note: Management was confident on top-line growth and the Seaways capacity build, but cautious on margins, citing fuel costs, ship start-up and depreciation, and admitted PAT was flat and ROCE muted; analysts pressed on the capex plan, debt rise and Seaways rate durability.
